articles.title: Inside the world of Filipino embalmers
articles.summary: Part 1: Embalmers preserve bodies of the departed for their loved ones to view them one last time

blocks.text: First of two parts
For 19 years now, 48-year-old Joycel Regalado has made a living by facing death.

She works on the remains of the departed, making sure that the memory of a beloved who has gone ahead of grieving family members is preserved. It is a final act of honoring that memory, of bringing comfort to the afflicted.

She had not always been interested in this kind of service — mortuary science, or the study of managing deceased human bodies. The closest she had been to it was helping with the processing of death certificates for the funeral services business of her relatives.
They persuaded her to get a license for embalmers so she could help in the business.

At age 23, she enrolled in an accredited Department of Health training program for embalmers and undertakers. On her first try, she passed the licensure exam and decided to head to Manila to try her luck. She left Bacolod to prove to her family that she wasn’t meant for just paperwork, and that she was actually capable of doing the work itself.
Joycel ended up with Arlington Memorial Chapels along Gregorio Araneta Avenue in Quezon City, armed with the necessary guts to do the job of respectfully handling the dead.
As senior embalmer at Arlington today, she has done services for more than a decade already, multiple times daily.
She still remembers her first time working on the remains of a baby. Already wearing her protective gear, she couldn’t help but weep with the bereaved family as she felt their anguish.

“Mahirap kasi nanay din ako.… [Pero] kahit umiiyak, gagawin ko…Iniisip ko na lang na kailangan ko itong gawin para ma-preserve din yung baby [at] makita siya ng mommy niya, ng pamilya niya,” she recalled.
(It was difficult because I am also a mother…. But even if I was crying, I did my job…I was thinking that I needed to do it to preserve the baby so the mother and family could still see the body.)

The task is not that different, day in and day out. She receives the body from the hospital, washes it thoroughly, sets the features of the face, drains the blood and injects formalin — the chemical that preserves the body — into the arteries. Organs are drained and formalin is injected into the body cavities to preserve the organs.

She double checks where fluids could leak from incisions in veins and arteries then stitches parts of the body. After she washes and dries the body, she grooms it, using a photograph of the deceased as her guide. Light cosmetics are applied to restore skin tone before the body is dressed in clothes provided by the family. It is finally put in a casket for viewing.
The entire process takes an average of two to four hours, in some cases possibly longer, depending on the body’s condition.
47-year-old, on-call embalmer RJ Cabillan has been in practice longer than Joycel. For him, it’s been almost 25 years of constantly seeing the dead at multiple funeral homes every week.
“Hindi na bago sa akin ’yung mga body, mga katawan ng pasyente, mga namamatayan. Kasi wala na, nasanay na ako,” he said.
(The bodies of patients and relatives of people who have passed away are nothing new to me. I’ve simply gotten used to it.)

blocks.caption: MORGUE. Embalmer RJ Cabillan shows some of the tools he regularly uses at Belmont Funeral Service – a trocar needle and an aspirating syringe, used to drain the body of fluids. Eirene Manatlao/Rappler

blocks.text: He had grown accustomed to being around bodies of the deceased since he had been accompanying his father — also an on-call embalmer — to work as early as age 9 or 10. By age 13, RJ began assisting his father in embalming the dead.
“That’s how I acquired the skills and eventually entered the field of embalming,” he said in a mix of English and Filipino.

After finishing high school, he first took on a construction job. But after he got weary of contractual setups, his father persuaded him to return to the embalming business. He did in 2001, and has never looked back since.
RJ found his way to Belmont Funeral Services in Novaliches, Quezon City, where he’s been working as resident embalmer for four years.

Like Joycel, RJ could not help tearing up while also embalming a baby. The experience, he said, reminded him of a personal tragedy — when three of his children passed away about two years apart, owing to pregnancy complications.
“Mapapaluha ka rin kahit anong tigas mo…Hindi mo maiiwasan ’yun.” (No matter how tough you are, you can’t help but end up in tears…There’s no avoiding it.)
No matter how difficult it was, RJ said he had to keep doing his job and pushing forward.
Years of experience have desensitized both Joycel and RJ to the sensory demands and anxieties of mortuary work.

Although both share the same job description as an embalmer, their daily routines differ based on the clientele they serve: Joycel works at a high-end facility, while RJ provides embalming services to low- and middle-income funeral homes.

As an in-house embalmer at Arlington, Joycel has a fixed shift schedule and focuses only on her areas of responsibility. RJ, for his part, waits for calls from four of the funeral homes he also serves.

Joycel has a fixed salary. Pay for senior embalmers can range from P25,000 to P30,000, depending on experience, on top of which is a benefits package that includes a rice subsidy, clothing and footwear allowance, routine medical checkups, and job-related hazard vaccinations. They have comprehensive machines, equipment, and a broader range of amenities.

blocks.caption: EQUIPMENT. Regalado uses an arterial injection pump (white equipment), along with other tools, to pump formalin through the arteries. Jake Gomez/Rappler

blocks.text: RJ, on the other hand, charges P1,000 per body for his services. There have been times when he has had to manually pump formalin because of the absence of automated machinery.

blocks.caption: MANUAL. Cabillan uses syringes and needles to manually pump formalin and drain bodily fluids. Eirene Manatlao/Rappler

blocks.text: Compared to other countries, their pay is extremely low, considering the hazards of the job. Joycel recalled preparing a corpse that had live worms in its legs. After an extremely repulsive experience, RJ now declines to embalm decomposed bodies.
Both work on four to six bodies a day, depending on the month. Joycel said work gets heavier during the hotter seasons.
Their counterparts in the US are paid much higher. In 2025, embalmers in the US received an average annual salary of P3.7 million* or around P300,000 a month.
Not many appreciate the work that embalmers do. Joycel said she has been asked, “Out of all the jobs out there, why is that your job?”
While embalming was once belittled as an occupation, Joycel said she aims to challenge that perception, emphasizing that embalmers complete formal studies and earn professional licenses.
When RJ was once asked how he is able to handle bodies of the deceased at work every day, he replied, “For me, that’s just normal. Given how long I’ve had this experience, I’m no longer afraid.”
Joycel asked: “Kung wala kami, sino ang mag-aayos ng patay?” (If we weren’t here, who would take care of the dead?)
She takes pride in her work. “Embalmers are still needed; embalmers are still in demand,” she said.
Her job has taught Joycel to value her time with the living.

“I realized that life is not just about work. I need to set aside time and balance for my family’s well-being, as well as for how I interact with others. Be kind, be understanding. Be good, and do good,” she said in a mix of English and Filipino.

RJ echoed the importance of time with family, adding that accepting death as a part of life is a better way to look at things. “Because we’ll arrive at the same outcome at some point in our lives,” he said.

For Joycel, her job as an embalmer is her ultimate good deed. “What we do for the deceased…We bring comfort to their families. We help lighten their [spirits]. That’s the only way I look at it.” (To be concluded) – Rappler.com

articles.title: MNLF denies protecting Bato dela Rosa
articles.summary: The Moro National Liberation Front denied speculations that it is coddling embattled Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is believed to be under the protection of an “armed and powerful group.”

blocks.text: Published November 2, 2026 2:16pm

The Moro National Liberation Front (MNLF) denied speculations that it is coddling embattled Senator Ronald “Bato” dela Rosa, who is believed to be under the protection of an “armed and powerful group.”

In a statement posted by the office of MNLF Chairman Muslimin Sema on Facebook on Sunday, the organization said that it has “no established formal relationship” with dela Rosa, and that its founder, Nur Misuari, is only a known “friend” of former president Rodrigo Duterte.
“The claim that the MNLF may be protecting him is speculation, not a confirmed fact,” the organization said.

“Dela Rosa appears to have personal and political connections to figures associated with the MNLF, especially through Duterte’s relationship with Nur Misuari, but there is no verified evidence that he is an MNLF member, ally in an operational sense, or currently being protected by the group,” it added.
The MNLF, however, cited reports that say that its organization is “fragmented” and that whether the Misuari faction would or could shield dela Rosa from arrest is “uncertain.”
It also cited claims that dela Rosa and Misuari may personally know each other, considering the latter’s ties with Duterte.

The Department of the Interior and Local Government has raised a P50-million reward for the arrest of dela Rosa, who according to Interior Secretary Juanito Victor "Jonvic" Remulla is now considered "armed and dangerous."
Remulla earlier said authorities were also negotiating with a group protecting the senator to secure his surrender and prevent a potentially violent confrontation.
The MNLF said that dela Rosa only publicly discussed their organization mainly in the context of conflict and peacebuilding.
“As a student in Marawi, he experienced fighting between government forces and the MNLF, and he has supported programs benefiting former combatants and their children,” the MNLF said.
“He has also advocated faster integration of qualified MILF and MNLF members into the PNP and AFP, indicating policy-level engagement rather than a personal or organizational tie,” it added.
GMA News Online reached out to the office of dela Rosa for a comment and will update this story once it responds.

Dela Rosa has been issued an arrest warrant from the International Criminal Court (ICC) in relation to the drug war of Duterte, which supposedly killed thousands of people. He was chief of the Philippine National Police at the time the war on drugs was implemented.
Duterte is already detained at the ICC in The Hague, Netherlands, while awaiting his crimes against humanity trial. —KG, GMA News

articles.title: Minns warns expected RBA rate rise will see ‘shops close that don’t reopen’ as pressure mounts on PM
articles.summary:
Frustration grows over the economy with one Labor MP saying voter anger is already high ahead of Reserve Bank of Australia decision

  • Get our

blocks.text: The NSW premier, Chris Minns, has warned an expected interest rate increase will force job losses and cause businesses to close, insisting the federal government and states should rein in spending to take pressure off the economy.
The intervention from the leader of the country’s biggest state will heap yet more pressure on the Albanese government ahead of the Reserve Bank of Australia’s cash rate decision on Tuesday.
Markets predict the bank will deliver the fifth rate rise in 2026. A move to 4.85% would bring rates to their highest level in 18 years.
Minns, who is increasingly outspoken on differences of opinion with the prime minister, Anthony Albanese, said increasing rates was not “a straightforward decision” for the RBA.
“The impact of another rate rise on the New South Wales economy will be massive,” Minns said.
“There’ll be jobs that go that will never come back. There’ll be shops that close that do not reopen with another rate rise.
“We can’t be flippant about this, this is a very, very tough call for them.”
Asked about government spending adding to inflation pressure, Minns said: “I think everybody needs to do their bit.”

Albanese and the treasurer, Jim Chalmers, have confirmed next month’s mid-year budget update will including a savings package, even as they point to international factors including the war in Iran as the cause of price hikes.
Internally, frustration is growing about the government’s handling of the economy.
One Labor MP told Guardian Australia voter anger was already high ahead of the rates decision, likening the tough political climate facing the government during a slump in polling in its first term.

They said Albanese and Chalmers would be hoping the trajectory for inflation and interest rates experienced before the 2025 election would play out again next year. After peaking at nearly 8% in late 2022, inflation fell to within the Reserve Bank’s target band before voters went to the polls.
“It’s the mid point in the cycle and people are grumpy,” the MP said.
Albanese will be at the commonwealth leaders’ summit in Antigua and Barbuda on Tuesday when the RBA announces its rates decision, leaving Chalmers to speak for the government.
The environment minister, Murray Watt, defended the government’s spending on Monday.
“We need to remember that Australia is not the only country going through inflationary pressures at the moment,” he told ABC radio.
“This is a global phenomenon, and even if the Australian government was to cut its budget to zero, we would still be experiencing inflationary pressures because of what’s happening around the world.”
after newsletter promotion
Labor frontbencher Tanya Plibersek defended Chalmers, insisting the savings would be meaningful but would not hurt households.
“There’s been no reforming treasurer in Australian history that hasn’t copped it when they’ve made big changes,” Plibersek said. “We all support Jim.”

blocks.caption: Inflation is ‘too high’, but RBA says Australia is not heading for recession – video

blocks.text: The ACTU secretary, Melissa Donnelly, warned workers “cannot survive another interest rate rise”, in a demonstration outside the RBA’s Sydney headquarters. She blamed big banks and supermarket giants for adding to the pressure on households by slugging customers.

“Workers are already struggling and feeling the brunt of these cost-of-living pressures. Workers didn’t create this inflationary crisis, it’s caused by Trump’s war in the Middle East, but workers are feeling the pain of it every day,” she said.

The Australian Council of Social Service chief executive, Cassandra Goldie, urged the RBA not to increase interest rates, calling instead for action to lower housing and energy prices and out of pocket medical costs.
“Higher interest rates create unemployment by design,” she said.

“We cannot be certain what the impact of another rate hike now will be on unemployment in a year’s time. An increase towards or above 5% would be disastrous, locking people out of jobs for years and forcing them to rely on grossly inadequate income support payments.”
Monday’s Newspoll put Labor’s primary vote at 27%, behind One Nation on 28%, but remaining ahead of the Coalition on 21%.
The opposition leader, Angus Taylor, accused the federal government of losing control of inflation and interest rates.
“We’re seeing a Labor government that can’t control its spending,” he said. “It cannot control its spending and the result of that is the Reserve Bank needs to do all the hard work.”

articles.title: World’s largest early warning system for severe child illness to launch in NHS A&Es across England
articles.summary:
Paediatric early warning system (Pews) uses a vital signs scoring system to assess whether a child is deteriorating

The world’s largest “early warning system” to spot when sick children are…

blocks.text: The world’s largest “early warning system” to spot when sick children are dangerously deteriorating is being introduced in A&E departments across England, NHS leaders have said.

The national paediatric early warning system (Pews) uses a scoring system for vital signs to assess whether a child needs more urgent attention. It is already used for inpatients, but NHS England has said this winter will be the first time it is used in A&E.

The mass rollout in England will make Pews the largest standardised scoring system in the world. Doctors and nurses can use it to measure, record and assess vital signs, such as blood pressure, heart rate, breathing rates, oxygen levels and consciousness.

A high score helps flag to medical staff when a child is deteriorating, though it was not designed to replace professional judgment or the input of parents, carers and children into a child’s condition, NHS England said.
Concerns raised can still trigger an immediate escalation of care, even if a child’s Pews score is low.
Duncan Burton, the chief nursing officer for England, said: “In fast-paced emergency departments, staff need to spot quickly when a child’s condition is deteriorating.
“This standardised approach will help them recognise the warning signs, communicate concerns, and make timely decisions when every moment matters.
“Just as importantly, it makes sure the concerns of children, parents and carers are heard and can prompt action.”
The Pews includes age-appropriate charts to reflect what may be abnormal signs of deterioration in babies, children and young people.
The scheme has also been designed specifically for A&E to help with rapid decision-making in busy environments.
More than 6 million children attend A&E in England each year. A similar process for adults, the national early warning system, is already used by NHS hospitals.
Separately, NHS England is drawing up urgent new standards for how children should be treated in A&E, including eliminating corridor care for youngsters as a priority.

Dr Mike McKean, the vice-president for policy at the Royal College of Paediatrics and Child Health (RCPCH), which worked on the new Pews system, said: “I am delighted to see this initiative being rolled out ahead of the winter period, which is always a busy and challenging time for hospitals and healthcare professionals.
“The emergency department Pews charts are extremely important tools that will support all paediatricians and wider child health teams to spot deterioration in children in hospital.
after newsletter promotion
“Alongside training and resources, it will help teams across England improve equity, patient safety and quality of care.”
Prof Lynn Woolsey, of the Royal College of Nursing, which was also involved in the work, said: “Early escalation is critical for keeping patients safe, particularly children.
“Already saving lives in other parts of the NHS, this system is a vital tool for nursing staff to quickly identify when a child patient is deteriorating, and act.

“The emphasis on listening to children, young people, parents and carers is especially important and having a standardised approach across emergency departments and paediatric wards will help support consistent assessment, communication and decision-making.
“It will be crucial to ensure there are enough nursing staff, with enough capacity, and the necessary training and support, to spot deterioration and use the system effectively.”
More than 90 hospitals across England use the national inpatient Pews system and data suggests they have consistently lower rates of cardiac arrests among their patients, according to NHS England.

articles.title: Millions in UK brace to remortgage on worse deals as rate rise looms
articles.summary:
More than 2.3m households face jump in payments in 2027, after expected increase in Bank of England rate this week

More than 2.3m UK households face a sharp rise in mortgage payments as they…

blocks.text: More than 2.3m UK households face a sharp rise in mortgage payments as they come off fixed-rate deals in 2027, with the Bank of England expected to begin raising interest rates this week.
The Bank’s nine-member monetary policy committee (MPC) is widely expected to increase the base rate from 3.75% to 4% on 5 November after UK inflation rose further to 3.5% in September.

It could be the first of four quarter-point rises over the next 12 months, according to financial market expectations, which would exacerbate the financial pressure on households grappling with higher energy and food bills.
Thousands of borrowers are due to come off fixed contracts in the final months of this year, with 700,000 having been forecast to switch over to new rates between July and December.
A further 2.3m households will reach the end of their fixed rates next year, according to data collected by UK Finance, a banking industry body.

There has been no change in the Bank of England base rate since December last year, but volatility in the bond markets – triggered in part by energy prices and inflation fears linked to the war in the Middle East – has driven up the swap rates that affect the pricing of fixed-rate mortgages.
An increase in the Bank of England rate could drive those rates, and wider household costs, even higher.
Data released last week showed that mortgage approvals in the UK fell to a near three-year low in September as potential buyers were deterred by the jump in borrowing costs.

Alongside last week’s budget, the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) warned that household disposable incomes would fall by 0.6% next year after taking account of inflation. The downgrade compares with the 0.6% increase in disposable incomes the watchdog had forecast in March – an outlook the OBR’s David Miles described as “a pretty grim picture”.
That income squeeze is also being driven by the energy price shock, which the OBR said would push consumer inflation to 3.5% this year, significantly higher than the 2% forecast in March.
Ofgem’s energy price cap, which determines household bills, is expected to rise by more than £400 in January, according to the latest forecast from EDF.

John Healey, the chancellor, made a £100 payout to 20m households the centrepiece of his budget, saying he wanted to “take the pressure off in the coldest months and see people through to the spring”.

His cost of living package – which also included cancelling fuel duty rises planned by Rachel Reeves and extending a VAT cut on electricity bills – was paid for by tax rises on banks, savers and landlords.

The Bank of England has taken a wait-and-see approach to rising inflation since the start of the Iran war, in contrast to other central banks, including the US Federal Reserve, Bank of Japan and European Central Bank, which have already raised borrowing costs this year.
after newsletter promotion

Andrew Bailey, the governor of the Bank of England, has made clear that the MPC is watching closely to see if rising prices are being passed through into higher wages for workers – evidence of the so-called “second-round effects” that can lead to inflation becoming embedded.
Before the war in the Middle East, the Bank had been expected to cut interest rates several times this year, with inflation expected to drift back down towards its 2% target.
But an extended period of historically high oil prices, affected by the closure of the strait of Hormuz choking off supplies, has instead fed through into high and rising inflation.
The Bank will publish updated forecasts for economic growth and inflation alongside its interest rate decision this week.
The UK economy beat expectations to be the joint fastest-growing in the G7 in the first half of 2026, which the Office for National Statistics said was partly driven by AI-related sectors.
But official forecasts for next year have been cut sharply amid fears that the higher cost of energy will eventually start to weigh on economic growth.
Although money market pricing suggests the Bank will raise interest rates four times by next July, many City economists suggest two rate rises are more likely.

articles.title: Most Israelis think settlements policy should change to avoid more sanctions, poll finds
articles.summary:
Survey finds UK government’s decision to impose trade ban was not a decisive factor in how Israelis voted in election

The UK government’s decision to impose a ban on trade in goods from…

blocks.text: The UK government’s decision to impose a ban on trade in goods from illegal settlements was not decisive in how Israelis voted in their general election, but a majority think the Israeli government’s settlements policy should change if it is going to lead to further sanctions, a new poll of Israelis shows.

There had been fierce criticism of the UK foreign secretary Ed Miliband’s decision in September to impose a trade ban and wider sanctions on illegal settlements, with some claiming it would drive Israeli voters into the arms of Benjamin Netanyahu.

A survey last month by Israeli social research group aChord shows overall support for foreign sanctions on violent settlers in the West Bank, but there was little support for the UK’s ban on trade with goods from illegal settlements, with many fearing it would end up being extended across Israel.

The survey is unique in showing how much the tougher line on Israel adopted by Britain and some foreign states was affecting the thinking of Israeli voters, and the extent to which Israelis thought it was a response to Israel’s actions or born of hostility to Israel, or even antisemitism.

The survey showed that three-quarters of supporters of the bloc backing Netanyahu said UK sanctions and trade ban policies towards Israel did not affect their vote at all, and to the small extent that they changed anyone’s vote, they shifted voters both ways, leaving no detectable net effect.

Just over three-quarters of all those surveyed (76) – had heard of the UK government announcement on settlements, even if 18 % had only heard the broad headline. Four-fifths of those that were aware of the announcement knew that the policy applied to the West Bank, and not the whole of Israel.

Israel’s relations with the west were “important or very important” to 60% of the supporters of the Change bloc of parties backing Gadi Eisenkot in deciding their vote. But even then these relationships came fifth in importance in a proffered group of six motives for voting. Only 30% of supporters of the Netanyahu bloc said relations with the west mattered in the same way.

But 71% of voters for the opposition Change bloc said the Israeli government should adapt its settlements policy to avoid an escalation of sanctions. Only 14% of Netanyahu bloc voters agreed, most saying instead that the government should continue the policy “whatever the price”.

A plurality of the public – 50% – said the settlement and construction policy in the West Bank should be adjusted to avoid sanctions escalation and international isolation, with 71% of Eisenkot bloc supporters agreeing to this proposition. Support for a change in the policy is strongest among supporters of the Arab parties.
after newsletter promotion

The finding prompted Hannah Weisfeld, the director of the British-Jewish organisation Yachad, to claim the research “illustrates that the Israeli public certainly recognises that if there is not a policy shift in relation to settlement enterprise, the international community is likely to try to create an incentive to shift things from the outside. If anything, that highlights the importance of UK and other allies taking action that targets the occupation.”

The survey also showed that concerns about foreign sanctions are highest when voters feel they will suffer a high personal price. Only 36% of all those surveyed agreed that the settlement policy should continue even if sanctions on banks that finance construction in illegal settlements led either to higher interest rates, difficulties in transferring money abroad, or using credit cards abroad. The poll suggests that the more people feel they will be damaged personally, the more they oppose the settlement policy.

A majority of all Israelis surveyed (52%) support sanctions on individual violent settlers, so long as the sanctions are imposed only on those acting violently, but 70% of Netanyahu bloc supporters oppose foreign sanctions in all circumstances.

There is much less widespread support for the policy of banning the import of goods from the illegal settlement, with 63% of all those surveyed opposing the ban and 26% either supporting the measure outright, or saying they would if it were underlined that the ban would not apply to goods from outside settlements.

articles.title: Israel has ‘historic’ opportunity to change direction, says leader of Arab coalition
articles.summary:
Yousef Jabareen says he is ready to join forces with opposition bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu after winning record number of seats in Knesset

The leader of Israel’s main Palestinian…

blocks.text: The leader of Israel’s main Palestinian coalition, which holds the balance of power after Tuesday’s elections, has said the country is facing a historic opportunity to change direction.
Yousef Jabareen, the head of the Joint List, said he was ready to join forces with the “Change” bloc to oust Benjamin Netanyahu and his far-right coalition, and to wrest control of the Knesset.

Turnout among Arab Israelis (Palestinians with Israeli citizenship, 20% of the population) more than doubled to about 80%, transforming the political landscape. Palestinians in the occupied West Bank and Gaza had no vote.

Jabareen said the first demand of the roughly 840,000 Palestinian Israeli voters was to get rid of the Netanyahu government, and in particular its most extreme members, Itamar Ben-Gvir, the national security minister, and Bezalel Smotrich, the finance minister.

“This has been an awful four years … in all areas of life: in terms of house demolition, criminal gangs within the Arab community without any [intervention] from the police; not allocating the needed resources for our municipalities, for our education, for our youth in general; racism in all areas of life – physical attacks against Arabs, the brutality of the police,” Jabareen told the Guardian in one of his first interviews since the election. “So this has been really a very dangerous period.”

He said the next few days would be critical. Israel’s president, Isaac Herzog, is due to summon political leaders as early as Wednesday to canvass their recommendations on who should be given the first chance to form the next government, with no single grouping commanding a clear claim on power.

Netanyahu’s coalition lost its majority, dropping from 68 to 53 seats in the 120-seat Knesset. The Change bloc of Zionist parties led by the retired general Gadi Eisenkot has 48 seats, leaving the Arab-Israeli parties as potential kingmakers with a record 19 seats. The Joint List has 11, while the more conservative, Islamist Ra’am has eight.

Eisenkot and his partners have pledged not to form a unity government with Netanyahu, but Eisenkot has also put conditions on any potential coalition with Arab parties: they have to recognise that Israel is a Jewish state, accept conscription, and denounce Hamas as a terrorist organisation.

Ra’am and its leader, Mansour Abbas, have signalled it is ready to join an Eisenkot coalition. The Joint List has no intention of joining such a government, but Jabareen said the coalition was ready to keep it afloat from the outside with tactical voting in the Knesset.

“The conditions that [Eisenkot] speaks of are more relevant for parties who would be in the coalition. We are not planning to be in the coalition … for very clear reasons,” Jabareen said at his family home in the northern city of Umm al-Fahm. “As long as the occupation of our people in the West Bank continues, we cannot be part of a government.

“However, in order to use our political power to get rid of the extreme Netanyahu government, we said that we will consider the possibility of supporting from outside. This is an opportunity to change policies, to change attitudes, including towards the Arab community and towards the Palestinian people.
“This is really a historic moment and I hope that there will be partners within the opposition to go ahead with that. We are thinking that this could be the start of a change.”

blocks.caption: Yousef Jabareen: ‘I hope we can find partners to make to make this change real’

blocks.text: Jabareen, 54, a former law professor and the leader of the socialist Hadash party, has yet to talk to Eisenkot since Tuesday’s elections, but he confirmed that informal discussions among opposition parties were under way.

Forming a new government was unlikely to be straightforward. The party leaders in the Change bloc have to agree on a candidate for prime minister. They would also have to accept partnership with Arab parties, either in coalition or from outside. The rightwing opposition leader, Avigdor Lieberman, is said to be the most resistant. Joint List officials said it was unclear whether partnership with Palestinians really crossed Lieberman’s red lines, or whether he was just holding out for a top cabinet position.

Even before a new government could be formed, Jabareen argued, the 67 opponents of Netanyahu in the new Knesset could use their clear majority to wrest control of legislative power. “That would start by changing the speaker of the Knesset,” he said, adding that the opposition could also take control of the committee that oversees the legislative agenda.

“That could be very crucially important … even before we reach conclusions on the issue of a coalition and a new government,” he said, adding that one of the priorities of the new Knesset should be to repeal laws passed by the outgoing majority that infringed the independence of Israel’s judiciary.
To allow an opposition coalition to oust Netanyahu and function as a minority government, Jabareen made clear it would also have to address deep-seated inequality in Israeli society.

“We have suffered from systemic discrimination for years, so if Eisenkot speaks of change, I believe that the change should come also for our community. We need to be treated equally,” he said. “We also ask for a political horizon. We would like to see the war stopped and the resumption of negotiation with the Palestinian leadership. We would like to see a start of a change.”

The Joint List leader said he was concerned over what Netanyahu might do to keep his grip on power. The prime minister has already made allegations, without evidence, that the Arab parties had used Qatari funds illegally in the election campaign, which Jabareen dismissed as a bid to “delegitimise the political power of the Arab community” and “a dangerous incitement”.
One of Jabareen’s concerns was that the Israeli leader would join Donald Trump in the resumption of war on Iran as a pretext for putting off political transition.
“This is really a critical period,” he said. “There should be a clear voice from the opposition to go against any attempt by him to initiate war … or dictate a new military agenda in Israel.”

articles.title: How a vampire drawing helped La Salle’s Joaquin Tovera vanquish rival Ateneo
articles.summary: ‘We hope that Joaquin stays to be that young guy who just enjoys basketball and doesn't care what the ramifications are of what he does,’ says La Salle coach Topex Robinson of Tovera, the standout…

blocks.text: HOTSHOTS. La Salle standouts JC Macalalag (left) and Joaquin Tovera celebrate a play against rival Ateneo in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament.
UAAP

‘We hope that Joaquin stays to be that young guy who just enjoys basketball and doesn't care what the ramifications are of what he does,’ says La Salle coach Topex Robinson of Tovera, the standout rookie who delivered another heroic performance for the defending UAAP champions

items: The Ateneo-La Salle rivalry in UAAP sports is characterized by heightened tension and pressure, prompting players and coaches to prepare more intensely.
Joaquin Tovera, a rookie player, showcased his skills by leading the La Salle team to a crucial overtime victory against Ateneo, scoring 21 points and demonstrating composure under pressure.
Tovera's teammates and coach praised his contributions and maturity, highlighting his ability to perform well despite the challenges faced by the team after the injury of a key player.

blocks.text: This is AI-generated. Read the article for full context. Report any errors.
MANILA, Philippines – For any Ateneo-La Salle rivalry in any UAAP sport, the tension and pressure are always more palpable than other games, no matter the current stakes.
Players and coaches alike sometimes prepare a bit more, spend more time mentally psyching themselves up, or simply do things they don’t normally do.
Joaquin Tovera idly draws on the coach’s whiteboard with a marker.

Ahead of one of the most crucial showdowns in the UAAP Season 89 men’s basketball tournament, the Blue Eagles and Green Archers found themselves locked with identical records squarely in the middle of the pack heading to Saturday, October 31.
The way the needle moves in this particular match could dictate how the rest of the season would go for either side.
Tovera, meanwhile, continued to draw, mimicking the vampire the La Salle team had set up in time for a chilling Halloween encounter.

Hours after drawing perhaps a pair of fangs or a cape, the 19-year-old dynamo was on the Araneta Coliseum court among thousands, this time drawing up winning plays for others or himself — his own fangs bared against Ateneo’s own scrappy band of brothers.

He traded the vampire’s cape for a hero’s one, as he eventually led the defending champions to an exhilarating 76-73 overtime win to the tune of 21 points, 7 rebounds, and 6 assists, and spent all the power he had before being helped off the floor after multiple bad ankle rolls.
Tovera did not care too much for roaring, clashing seas of blue and green around him, for the game was like his drawing on the board before the game: simply black and white. Win, or lose.

Head coach Topex Robinson, who saw Tovera scribbling before the rivalry match and joked if the soft-spoken guard was planning to take over his job, emphasized this defining moment as to why his rookie is just on a different lane as the rest.

“I was like, ‘Do you know how important this game is again?’ [He said] ‘Yes coach, but I love to draw,’” Robinson recounted post-game. “We hope that Joaquin stays to be that young guy who just enjoys basketball and doesn’t care what the ramifications are of what he does.”

“We’re just so fortunate that he has a good support system with these guys. Every time he makes a mistake, you’ll always see one of them trying to pacify him. We’re so fortunate to have these guys guiding in his rookie year. Hopefully, he gets to appreciate the support that he gets.”
Never mind the pressure of righting a title defense gone sideways early. Never mind the pressure of needing to step up right as your mentor and leader goes down.

In the two games since graduating star Jacob Cortez went down with an injury, the Fil-Am youngster from NBA player breeding ground Chino Hills in California has averaged MVP-caliber numbers of 18 points, 7 rebounds, and 7.5 assists on 44% shooting.

Though potential has always been there the moment Tovera stepped into the UAAP, this is the first stretch of games where his grace under pressure has been truly tested, especially after the Archers went down with an alarming 3-4 record to end the first round before rebounding to 6-4.
Ever a kid of few words, Tovera simply said he wanted to do what’s best for the team, and essentially hold the fort while Cortez recovers for the final stretch of his collegiate career.
His La Salle kuyas, however, have much more to say about his character, extending well beyond his years.

“He’s been huge for us these past three games. He’s had really good contributions,” said veteran guard JC Macalalag. “I just tried to remind him of what he can do. Being able to facilitate the team and control the tempo at a young age leaves a lot of room for improvement.”
“For me, it’s just his composure that really stands out the most, with how he’s able to stay poised under pressure,” added former Ateneo prospect Mason Amos.

“Time and time again, he tends to deliver for us, and as a kuya, I’m really proud of his efforts, and proud of him not getting emotional when things get rough for him. He just keeps moving forward and that’s something that I can really say about Joaquin.” – Rappler.com

articles.title: US envoy reaffirms PH alliance 'stronger than ever' after ASEAN defense meet
articles.summary: United States Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton on Monday reaffirmed Washington"s commitment to Philippine security, describing it as “ironclad” and the two countries" alliance as “stronger…

blocks.text: Published November 2, 2026 1:16pm

United States Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton on Monday reaffirmed Washington’s commitment to Philippine security, describing it as “ironclad” and the two countries’ alliance as “stronger than ever.”
Lipton issued the statement following the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus in Cebu, which was attended by US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth.
“I want to reaffirm the United States’ enduring commitment to the Philippines and our shared vision for a peaceful, secure, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Lipton said.

He said Hegseth’s frequent engagements with Southeast Asian partners demonstrate the Trump administration’s “determination to strengthen alliances, deepen regional cooperation, and ensure that peace is backed by strength.”
Statement to the People of the Philippines https://t.co/7Lz4p0EJtn— U.S. Ambassador Lee Lipton (@USAmbPH) November 2, 2026
Lipton added that the visits of the US Secretary of War also underscore the importance Washington places on Southeast Asia and its alliance with the Philippines.

“Our commitment to Philippine security is ironclad. With President Ferdinand Marcos Jr., the United States and the Philippines have built a powerful partnership grounded in shared principles, mutual respect, and an unwavering commitment to regional stability,” Lipton said.
“As we mark 75 years of the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty, our message is clear: our alliance is stronger than ever,” he added.

Lipton also emphasized Washington’s long-term commitment to the partnership, particularly its support for defending Philippine sovereignty, protecting the country’s territorial integrity, and upholding freedom of navigation.

Beyond defense cooperation, the US envoy said the security partnership should be matched by an equally strong economic relationship, stressing Washington’s support for the Philippines’ economic development.

“The United States is proud to call the Philippines an ally, partner, and friend. Our relationship is not simply a matter of treaties or shared strategic interests; it is a bond between our peoples that grows stronger every day,” Lipton said.

During the ASEAN-United States Defense Ministers’ Informal Meeting, Hegseth proposed developing a framework for defense cooperation between Washington and ASEAN in recognition of the 50th anniversary of US-ASEAN relations.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: End of Sara Duterte impeachment trial 'possible' in November, says prosecution
articles.summary: The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte could wrap up by the end of November if the defense presents its evidence within 10 full trial days, House lead prosecutor and Batangas Rep.…

blocks.text: Published November 2, 2026 1:02pm

The impeachment trial of Vice President Sara Duterte could wrap up by the end of November if the defense presents its evidence within 10 full trial days, House lead prosecutor and Batangas Rep. Gerville Luistro said.

In a statement, Luistro raised the possibility after the House prosecution panel on October 13 dropped three of the four Articles of Impeachment against Duterte, which covered allegations of misuse of confidential funds, bribery and grave threats.
The defense team had originally sought 30 trial days to present its evidence on all four Articles of Impeachment under the pretrial order.
“Posible po na matapos ito bago ang katapusan ng Nobyembre,” Luistro said.
(It’s possible that the trial will conclude before the end of November.)
“We have reason to believe na ito pong 30 trial days na ito ay malaki ang mababawas. Sana kalahati na lang o sampu na lang,” she added.
(We have reason to believe that these 30 trial days will be significantly reduced. Hopefully, only half or 10 days will be needed.)
Luistro, however, said the final trial schedule would remain subject to the approval of the Senate impeachment court and the number of witnesses the defense intends to present.
If the defense requires more than the expected 10 full trial days, the proceedings could extend into December.
“But at any rate, we are all hoping and praying na sana naman bago mag-Pasko ay tapos na ang impeachment trial na ito para magkaroon tayo ng closure, and we can all move on,” Luistro said.
(But at any rate, we are all hoping and praying that the impeachment trial will be over before Christmas so we can have closure, and we can all move on.)
The impeachment trial is currently suspended to give way to Senate committee deliberations on the proposed 2027 national budget.
The Senate impeachment court is scheduled to reconvene on November 9 at 10 a.m.

With the decision to drop three Articles of Impeachment, the prosecution will pursue only Article II, which concerns allegations that Duterte failed to fully declare her assets and divest from business interests, raising questions about her unexplained wealth.

Defense lead counsel Sheila Sison earlier said the move would not affect the defense panel's presentation of evidence, stressing that Duterte should still be allowed to address allegations already presented before the impeachment court.

“That prerogative to withdraw an accusation is not the power to suppress its rebuttal on the part of the respondent. The authority to streamline, or to achieve speed in a trial, is not the authority to diminish due process, or to altogether disregard fundamental rules of fairness," Sison said.
"And the desire to reach a verdict expeditiously can never justify reaching it unfairly,” she added.— MCG, GMA News

articles.title: Counsellors and psychotherapists call for UK statutory regulation in ‘watershed moment’
articles.summary:
Exclusive: Professional bodies call for regulation to boost confidence and protect public from abuse in ‘landmark’ report

Ministers should introduce statutory regulation for counsellors and…

blocks.text: Ministers should introduce statutory regulation for counsellors and psychotherapists to protect the public from abuse, according to a report that has been hailed as a “watershed moment” for the profession.
Unlike most other healthcare roles, including doctors, midwives and osteopaths, “psychotherapist” and “counsellor” are not protected titles nor statutorily regulated professions in the UK.

This means that anyone can call themselves a therapist without a qualification, and can continue to practise even after an episode of misconduct, under a system that is poorly understood by the public.

For the first time, the professional bodies that represent counsellors and psychotherapists, and which run the current voluntary accreditation scheme, are calling for statutory regulation to boost confidence in the profession and protect the public from the growing number of cases of abuse and malpractice.

The report, the culmination of an independent review launched in October 2025 by the Commission for the Future of Counselling and Psychotherapy, argues that counsellors and psychotherapists are an untapped resource that could fill a mental health treatment gap estimated at about 1.8 million people on waiting lists. Practitioners told the commission they had extra capacity, which the report estimated could cumulatively provide more than 370,000 hours of additional therapy appointments every week.

The commission co-chair Phil Hope, a former Labour minister for care services, said: “For me, the report became a bit of a watershed moment for the profession, a real landmark of the opportunity there is for the government, and all its departments really, to unlock that potential.”

blocks.caption: Ella Janneh: ‘Your Friday night kebab is subject to stronger regulation than a therapist who sits in rooms alone with vulnerable people.’ Photograph: Ella Janneh

blocks.text: Ella Janneh, who successfully sued her therapist in the high court for rape and sexual assault in 2024, and has campaigned for regulation with the support of the law firm Leigh Day, welcomed the “collective call for regulation”. She said it had taken “years and a lot of honest and difficult conversations between victims, other campaigners and conscientious professionals”.

“Statutory regulation would lock abusive and unethical people out of the system. The current lack of centralised regulation allows for repeat offenders to continue practising with no oversight. That is reason enough to bring in regulation,” Janneh said.

The report cites her “powerful testimony” as an illustration of the “devastating, ongoing impact” the absence of statutory regulation can have, since her therapist is still able to practise despite the outcome of her civil case.

“One of the main reasons why the lack of government regulation has skated under the radar of public awareness,” said Janneh, “is that most people assume it’s already in place. They only realise it’s not when something’s gone wrong … Currently your Friday night kebab is subject to stronger regulation than a therapist who sits in rooms alone with vulnerable people.”

The report’s co-chair Andrea Sutcliffe, the former chief executive of the Nursing and Midwifery Council and an expert on regulation, said: “We’ve been on a journey around regulation with counselling and psychotherapy over many, many, many years, and the coalition government set its face against statutory regulation in 2011.

“We heard some really powerful testimony about the risk and the fact that people have been harmed. What the government asks for is a compelling case for statutory regulation because it costs and [it’s not] an easy thing to do … but as independent co-chairs, we feel that a compelling case exists.”

blocks.caption: Andrea Sutcliffe, a co-chair of the report, said ‘a compelling case’ existed for statutory regulation of counselling and psychotherapy.  Photograph: Linda Nylind/The Guardian

blocks.text: Regulation was especially important for counselling and psychotherapy because they were complex interventions requiring years of training to practise, Sutcliffe said. Therapy takes place in a one-on-one setting; most practitioners are independent, meaning there is no employer oversight; and their patients are typically vulnerable people.

“People are in difficult, vulnerable situations, why would we expect them to be experts in working out who they should go to and who is safe? That’s not what we do for choosing a brain surgeon or a cardiologist. We expect those things,” she said, adding that the lack of regulation contributed to misconceptions and mistrust, which prevented people from seeking help.

Regulation would also be helpful in setting standards for education, training and development, Sutcliffe said. The report noted that this would also improve diversity in the profession, which is much needed.

The report further argues that the evidence base for counselling and psychotherapy should be improved, and notes that its lack is resulting in “insufficient and unsustainable public commissioning and investment”. Hope said commissioners in the NHS and local government often had “legitimate concerns, is this a qualified psychotherapist or not?”

A more coordinated, professionalised industry could better inform the government’s approach to regulation and guardrails around the growing use of AI for mental health support. “[Psychotherapists are] seriously concerned at the risk that people may be accessing services that are totally unregulated. And therefore, the profession needs, I think, to up its game a bit and move up the pace here because this is happening,” said Hope.

The commission hopes the report’s call will be taken up by policymakers. The Labour MP Sojan Joseph, the chair of the all-party-parliamentary group on mental health and a former nurse, said he supported the case for statutory regulation and would raise the issue in parliament.

Jon Levett, the UK Council for Psychotherapy’s chief executive officer, said he would welcome statutory regulation that “protects the public, sets clear standards and preserves people’s choice of therapy”, though he argued that “any new system must be developed with practitioners and people with lived experience”.

Dr Lisa Morrison, the British Association for Counselling and Psychotherapy’s chief regulation and standards officer, agreed that collaboration was key to ensure regulation “places public protection, public benefit and public confidence at its heart, while avoiding barriers to access, diversity and established practice”.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli makes history as youngest F1 champion
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion and Italy's first since 1953 when he finished third in Sunday's thrilling and crash-hit Mexico City Grand Prix.

image.caption: Four-time champion Max Verstappen and seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton hoist Kimi Antonelli aloft as a carnival of celebrations began after the Mexico City Grand PrixImage: Eloisa Sanchez/REUTERS

blocks.text: Kimi Antonelli became Formula One's youngest world champion at 20 years and 68 days old on Sunday when he finished third in the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton.
The previous recordholder was Germany's Sebastian Vettel, who first became a world champion at age 23 in 2010.
Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953.
"I'm speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened," said Antonelli after finishing the race.
His parents and sister were there to embrace him when he stepped out of the car.
He was then mobbed by his pit crew.

blocks.caption: Antonelli is also the first Italian champion since 1953Image: Claudia Greco/REUTERS

blocks.text: 'An incredible season'
"It's been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max ​and Lewis is truly incredible. And looking forward to some more battles in the future," the 20-year-old said.
Antonelli, who secured the title with four races remaining, said the final lap was complicated by the excitement of what he had achieved.

"I think I lost two seconds because I could not see ahead, I think I saw two Ferraris," he said. "It was very special, a lot of memories went through my mind at that moment, and I let it all out after achieving one of my biggest dreams."
Antonelli has now risen to 380 points with four races remaining. Verstappen (261) snuck past Hamilton (259) in the standings, but they will be racing for second the rest of the ​way.

blocks.caption: Antonelli said the final lap was complicated by the excitement of what he had achievedImage: Daniel Becerril/REUTERS

blocks.text: Antonelli started the race in ​fourth and needed to finish ‌ninth or better to secure the championship on Sunday no matter what his peers did.
He had a relatively smooth run, though the race was interrupted by a red flag around Lap ​45 when Valtteri Bottas crashed.
Verstappen, meanwhile, claimed his sixth victory at the Mexico City Grand Prix, further cementing his affinity with the circuit.
After Mexico, F1 will head to Brazil and then to Las Vegas.
The final two Grands Prix are scheduled to be held in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. But it remains uncertain whether they will take place, given the geopolitical instability in the region.

articles.title: South Korea to pour billions into AI
articles.summary: South Korea to spend billions to strengthen the country's technological edge.

image.caption: South Korean President Lee Jae Myung leaves after delivering a budget speech for 2027 at the National Assembly in Seoul.Image: Lee Jin-man/REUTERS

blocks.text: South Korea will pour nearly $16 billion on artificial intelligence and semiconductors, South Korea's President Lee Jae Myung said in his annual budget address to parliament.

"We will invest 21.3 trillion won (€14.3 billion, $15.97 billion), nearly twice ​this year's amount, in AI and the three megaprojects of semiconductors, physical ​AI and ‌AI data centres," Lee said on Monday.
He added that 4.7 trillion won will be invested to bolster "frontier AI development projects, with the aim of achieving world-leading performance for our own AI model, a national strategic asset."
South Korea unveils record budget proposal for 2027
The Lee administration has unveiled a record budget proposal for next year, featuring a 12.8% increase in government spending to 820.9 trillion won (€551.5 billion, $615.62 billion).
The proposal needs parliamentary approval, and Lee's party, the Democratic Party of Korea (DPK), currently holds the majority.
South Korea is Asia's fourth-largest economy and home to two of the world's biggest memory chip makers — Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
The AI boom has sent demand for memory chips soaring.
South Korea recorded faster-than-expected economic growth in the third quarter, driven by chip exports and investment.

Exports totaled $930 billion from January to October and are on track to surpass $1 trillion this year, making South Korea the fourth country to achieve the milestone after the United States, China and Germany.

articles.title: UK making up China policy ‘as it goes along’, MPs warn
articles.summary:
Commons committee says lack of coherent strategy is hampering business and leaving national security risks unaddressed

The UK is making up policy on China “as it goes along” and risks having…

blocks.text: The UK is making up policy on China “as it goes along” and risks having its strategy dictated by Washington or Beijing, a parliamentary report has concluded.

An investigation by the Commons business, innovation, science and trade select committee said Labour’s failure to formulate a coherent strategy since 2024 “combined the worst of both worlds” for the UK in relation to China.
Liam Byrne, Labour MP and chair of the committee said the UK’s policy on China meant it was also endangering its business with the EU with the risk of being “cut off” from big manufacuring contracts.
The government could neither deliver commercial opportunities to British businesses nor control the “increasing exposure to unquantified, managed risk” in relations with China, it found.
The report said: “In 2024, the new government promised a strategic, long-term, consistent UK approach to China. It has not delivered on this.
“Britain must shape its own relationship with China or risk having that relationship shaped for us in Washington or Beijing.”
The UK’s relationship with China has been marked by a lack of engagement in the last 10 years, with Keir Starmer making the first official visit in January since Theresa May in 2018.

That trip was billed as an effort to end the “diplomatic ice age”, but since 2018 China has benefited from an export boom that is now fuelling fears about deindustrialisation, adding to deep-seated existing concerns about cyber espionage and national security.

The MPs acknowledged the advantages of trading with Beijing in their report, noting that British businesses have profitable operations in China and “are ambitious to grow” and learn from the country’s “world-leading” innovations.
At the same time, consumers benefit from low-cost imports when household incomes are squeezed, with electric vehicles being a case in point.
However, Byrne sharply criticised the government’s piecemeal approach.
“Britain’s businesses cannot plan for the future when the government keeps making up its China policy as it goes along.
“Ministers promised clarity and consistency. Instead, we have opportunities missed, risks unmanaged and decisions left until the 11th hour.”
The committee cited the decision in March to block the Chinese firm Ming Yang from building a £1.5bn wind energy plant in Scotland after years of negotiation because of unspecified security risks.
Scotland’s first minister, John Swinney, has called on Andy Burnham to reconsider Starmer’s decision.
That decision, along with the emergency takeover of British Steel from its Chinese owners, “has been characterised by reactivity, inconsistency and opacity”, the report said.

Work on a new strategy, the committee said, should be combined with official preparations for new trade remedies to counter unfair competition, including potential tariffs on EVs, something Downing Street has not ruled out.

The report calls for “clear new rules of the game” and recommends the designation of a “red zone” for industries that would be off-limits for Chinese investment and a “green zone”, where trade should be encouraged.
Byrne said a China strategy was an urgent concern as “Europe is changing fast” and “proposing new trade protections as it gets bolder with Beijing and warier of Washington”.
The new laws “may trap Britain outside EU trade walls, cutting us off from our largest market”.

Byrne said the government “should be prepared to consider dynamic alignment” with the EU include tariffs on EVs “as the price of securing British firms a place in the EU’s Made in Europe project” and to help guard against China dominance.
The UK is already under pressure to align with the EU on tariffs on EVs, but the business secretary, Jonathan Reynolds, has said he will make a decision in the best interests of the UK.

The EU has already imposed tariffs on Chinese EVs, capped the number of hybrid cars that can be imported from China and is now considering a Franco-German proposal for a “kill switch” to block imports if China weaponises trade – as it did last year with curbs on exports of rare-earth minerals and chips. “The UK’s partners are moving further and faster,” the report noted.
China is now on track to surpass last year’s record $1.19tn trade surplus with the rest of the world.

Its latest five-year plan, covering 2026 to 2030, gives a glimpse of where China is going next in prioritising the strategic expansion of high-value green exports such as EVs, batteries, wind turbines, hydrogen and solar panels.

articles.title: PH Red Cross attends to over 8,700 patients during Undas 2026
articles.summary: The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) on Monday said it has attended to 8,721 patients nationwide since October 29 amid the observance of Undas 2026.

blocks.text: Published November 2, 2026 12:48pm
The Philippine Red Cross (PRC) on Monday said it has attended to 8,721 patients nationwide since October 29 amid the observance of Undas 2026.
Based on the PRC's latest operational report as of 9 a.m. on Monday, all 8,721 patients received vital signs monitoring.
The PRC said 359 were classified as minor cases, while 19 were considered major cases.
The minor cases included dizziness, headaches, lacerations, abrasions, insect bites, difficulty breathing, sprains, burns, hypertension, fever, and injuries sustained in motorcycle crashes.
Major cases included chest pain, seizures, suspected stroke, cardiac arrest, heat stroke, and difficulty breathing.
According to the PRC, nine patients were brought to hospitals due to conditions such as stroke, body weakness, loss of consciousness, and hypoglycemia.
A total of 297 welfare assistance services were also provided, including psychological first aid, referrals, tracing services, and the distribution of hot meals and food packs.
Other forms of assistance included wheelchair services for 25 individuals, water provision for 149 people, and the distribution of information and education materials.
For its Undas operations, the PRC deployed 1,977 personnel nationwide, composed of 132 staff members and 1,845 volunteers.
Its deployed assets included 73 ambulances, 404 first aid stations, 131 welfare desks, 45 foot patrols, 32 mobile units, and other service vehicles and equipment.

Cemeteries accounted for the largest number of PRC mobilization areas with 349 deployment points nationwide. Other areas included bus terminals, highways, seaports, beaches, airports, and gas stations.
The PRC's Undas Operation 2026 runs from October 29 to November 3. — Joviland Rita/RSJ, GMA News

blocks.text: DUTERTE. Former president Rodrigo Duterte personally attends the third status conference on his case at the International Criminal Court in the Hague, Netherlands, on September 16, 2026.
ICC-CPI
The conference comes weeks before the opening of Duterte's trial scheduled on November 30
MANILA, Philippines – The International Criminal Court (ICC) will hold its fifth status conference on former Philippine president Rodrigo Duterte’s crimes against humanity case on Monday, November 2.
This comes weeks before the opening of the trial scheduled on November 30.
A status conference is where parties discuss matters related to the case before proceeding to a full trial.

So far, the court has had four conferences: on May 27, when it announced that the trial will begin on November 30; on June 23, when the chamber cautioned lawyers against granting media interviews; and the third one, on September 16, when the former president made an appearance.
The court held the fourth conference on October 13, where the parties discussed the list of evidence anew.
Duterte will skip the Monday hearing after waiving his right to be present.
For the fifth status conference, the Trial Chamber III and the parties will discuss the following:

items: Audio-visual link testimony and rights of audience
List of witnesses and number of hours for the Prosecution’s presentation of evidence
Potentially exculpatory evidence, agreed facts, and calling order
Rule 68(3) applications and in-court protective measures

articles.title: China says Gibo gave Beijing less than five working days’ notice for ASEAN defense talks
articles.summary: China has accused Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. of blocking its participation in last week’s ASEAN defense talks in Cebu, claiming that the Philippines invited China to join the talks…

blocks.text: November 2, 2026 | 12:19pm
China's Defence Attache to the Philippines Yang Lei attends the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus) in Cebu on October 29, 2026.
Eloisa Lopez, pool via AFP

MANILA, Philippines — China has accused Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. of blocking its participation in last week’s ASEAN defense talks in Cebu, claiming that the Philippines invited China to join the talks only after pressure from other Southeast Asian states.

In a statement posted on Facebook late Sunday, November 1, the Chinese Embassy in Manila claimed Teodoro “acted out of personal self-interest” and disregarded the principle of openness and inclusivity of the ASEAN Defense Ministers’ Meeting-Plus (ADMM-Plus), which the Philippines hosted in Cebu on October 28 and 29.

“Only after other ASEAN countries expressed strong opposition to such acts that the Philippines Department of National Defense (DND) reluctantly sent an invitation letter to China on October 22,” the embassy said, adding that the letter was signed by an undersecretary “who was unwilling to even put a date on the letter.”
Philstar.com has reached out to Teodoro for comment. This report will be updated with his response.
The allegation follows remarks by China's defense ministry spokesperson on October 29, who alluded to a "Philippine politician" who allegedly obstructed China's participation in the talks.

During a press conference in Beijing, Zhang Xiaogang told reporters that the Philippines had allowed “a certain self-serving politician to act recklessly” and use its chairmanship to block China’s participation, but he did not name Teodoro.
The embassy said all other ADMM-Plus members received their invitations in late September or early October.

"On October 23, Teodoro said in a press conference that China had been sent notice only the previous day," the embassy said. "It left China fewer than five working days for preparation. China was also required to complete its registration within just two days."
"Under such circumstances, it was virtually impossible to complete the necessary preparation," it added.
At his October 23 briefing, Teodoro said the Philippines had sent an invitation to Beijing through a letter signed by Defense Undersecretary Ignacio Madriaga.
Four days later, DND spokesperson Arsenio Andolong confirmed that an invitation had been sent but China had yet to confirm its representative.
Beijing eventually sent Senior Capt. Yang Lei, its defense attaché in Manila, instead of its defense minister, marking China's lowest level of representation at the forum since its launch in 2010.
Teodoro personally welcomed the other delegation heads at the venue but did not greet Yang, who was instead received by Madriaga.
Teodoro said there should be parity in rank, and that an undersecretary welcoming an attaché was “more than courteous.”
The embassy did not identify which ASEAN countries that had supposedly objected to the Philippines’ handling of the invitation.
Zhang made a similar claim last week, but Teodoro dismissed it as Beijing’s view rather than that of ASEAN.
“So it is China’s position, it is not ASEAN’s position,” Teodoro said at the close of the meetings.

articles.title: ‘I want to slap you around a bit, too’: Victorian magistrate reprimanded over language in court
articles.summary:
Judicial commission finds against Vicky Prapas over a series of comments, including one made when school children were present

  • Get our

blocks.text: A magistrate who told a court user “I want to slap you around a bit, too” has come under fire for her offensive and inappropriate language.
The remark was one of several made by Victorian magistrate Vicky Prapas that the state’s judicial watchdog has found to be inappropriate.
Others included asking someone in court: “Do you reckon the substance is screwing with the way you’re thinking?” and asserting that another person “believes their own bullshit”.
The latter comment was made in the presence of a school group, the judicial commission of Victoria said in its findings last week.
The watchdog opened the investigation after receiving a complaint from Victoria Legal Aid concerning Prapas’ rotation through a Melbourne drug court.

The investigation substantiated a range of allegations, including that the magistrate made threatening or intimidating remarks to legal practitioners when they proposed to make or support complaints against her.
Those comments amounted to a “pattern of victimisation”, the commission found.
Prapas was also found to have made an offensive comment about a person from a marginalised group and made an unprofessional remark about another member of the judiciary.

In the written decision, Prapas acknowledged, among other things, that her conduct in some instances had been “unfiltered and intemperate” and that she would have expressed herself differently with the benefit of hindsight.
But she referred to the unique jurisdiction of a drug court, including that her intention was to promote participant recovery, accountability and community safety within its therapeutic framework.
She said she had reflected carefully on the matters raised, and had taken steps to ensure that her communication remained effective, respectful and less susceptible to misunderstanding.
after newsletter promotion
The watchdog was unable to substantiate some allegations, including that the magistrate demonstrated cultural insensitivity.
In handing down its findings, the commission acknowledged drug court proceedings can warrant “open and frank” discussions.
“However, these features do not displace a judicial officer’s obligation to afford all court users civility and respect,” it said.
The brunt of the complaint was referred to the chief magistrate, Lisa Hannan, with recommendations she counsel Prapas.
The watchdog also recommended Prapas familiarise herself with the commission’s conduct guidelines and attend an educational event within a year.

articles.title: In Mountain Province, a solemn path of smoke and fire honors the dead
articles.summary: In Sagada, lighting fires on graves serves as an act of remembrance meant to warm and guide the spirits of departed loved ones

blocks.text: SAGADA, Philippines – Traced back to the arrival of the Anglican mission in the early 1900s, this unique tradition has deeply influenced local culture and beliefs in the Mountain Province.

Panag-apoy, a solemn practice observed by Sagada locals every November 1, All Saints’ Day, honors the dead through smoke and fire. It is also known as “Pagdedenet,” a Kankanaey term meaning “to light the fire.”
The lighting of fire on graves holds meaning for both tribal and Anglican beliefs, serving as an act of remembrance meant to warm and guide the spirits of departed loved ones.
Panag-apoy starts with a Holy Mass to remember the departed members of the community. In some towns across the province, names of the deceased locals are read aloud during the service.
The local priest then blesses the graves, including candles and flowers at the cemetery, signaling locals to light their saeng or saleng — small bundles of fatwood placed on top of graves.
As the fire burns, the cemetery glows orange as smoke fills the sky.

blocks.caption: The fire from each grave commemorates a soul who was once part of the local community. Photo by Jyor So

blocks.text: Locals and officials stress that Panag-apoy is not a festival, despite the influx of tourists in recent years due to social media posts.
While residents appreciate visitors, the swelling crowds, they say, have disrupted the solemnity and sacredness of the tradition.

blocks.caption: The light burning the fatwood is believed to be the light of Jesus guiding the souls of the departed. Photo by Kenosis Yap

blocks.text: This year, the local government of Sagada limited visitor access to preserve the solemnity of the occasion. Tourists may only observe the practice from 7 pm to 9 pm, and drone cameras are not allowed.

blocks.caption: Tourists quietly take photos of the sacred practice. Photo by Jyor So

blocks.text: The ritual unfolds in silence as the youth watch their elders light the saeng, passing the sacred tradition to the next generation.

blocks.caption: Even late at night, locals continue to arrive and light up fires for their loved ones. Photo by Kenosis Yap.

articles.title: Million-dollar fish caught by Darwin man ‘just fishing and talking’ at night with brother
articles.summary:
‘I’m just happy to catch fish,’ Matthew Maurice says after landing 80cm barramundi as part of Northern Territory competition

  • Get our

blocks.text: A Darwin man is $1m richer after angling an 80cm, red-tagged barramundi during a night-time fishing trip with his brother.
Matthew Maurice, a 26-year-old from the Northern Territory, had finished football training and decided to take a boat out on Thursday evening with his sibling, who was visiting from overseas.
“We couldn’t be bothered going too far, we only went less than a kilometre from the boat ramp,” Maurice told Channel 7’s Sunrise on Monday.
“We just wanted to fish and talk, that was the only thing. Whether we caught fish or not, it didn’t matter. We just wanted to be together.”

Maurice managed to snag a barramundi that night, but what he saw when the creature’s silvery body jumped out of the water got his blood pumping: a bright red tag signalling a big win in the NT’s Million Dollar Fish competition.
“I hooked up to the fish and my first reaction was to turn my head torch on, the first thing that lit up was pretty much a big silver body and a big red tag hanging out of it,” he said.
As part of the competition, 100 fish – each carrying prize money of $10,000 – were released into waterways for the competition, which began 1 October, alongside the one, elusive top prize.
It was only after he turned in his catch that Maurice discovered the red tag on his barramundi carried the million-dollar prize.
“I’m about to give you the best news of your life,” the NT’s chief minister, Lia Finocchiaro, reportedly told the man.
Maurice later called his mother and brother to share the news, adding he plans to do something “smart” with his winnings.
“I’m just happy to catch fish. I can’t believe I caught a million dollars’ worth of fish,” Maurice said during a press conference.
“Any barra is a good barra, especially the million-dollar one.”

“I feel like I’m in a dream,” he went on. “I don’t think I should be allowed to touch the money. Someone else might need to look after it for me. But I’ll probably be smart with it, buy a house, pay off anything I need to pay off, and then treat myself a little bit.”
Maurice has become the second person in the competition’s 12-year history to win the top prize. A local man from Katherine, Keegan Payne, snagged a $1m fish three years ago.
The initiative is a program sponsored by Tourism & Events Northern Territory, meant to tout the region’s “world-class fishing experiences”.
The competition continues until 31 March 2027, with dozens of tagged barramundi worth a $10,000 bounty left to be caught in regions across the Top End, with 96 yet to be claimed.
